title: Occult mediate revelation binds by accompanying signs
pass_a_gloss: XXI. Occult is that by which God through his ambassadors signifies something as divine to others in such a way that he employs certain signs, by whose efficacy he drives those to announce, but binds these to believe. Thus God through Moses to Pharaoh by various signs, Exodus chapters 7-10; through Jeremiah to his people he foreshadows their coming ruin by a girdle, Jeremiah 13. Such is the barber's razor, Ezekiel 5:1. Such the marriage with a harlot, Hosea 1:2.
pass_b_english: XXI. It is occult when God, through his ambassadors, signifies something as divine to others and also employs certain signs — signs whose force drives the messengers to announce and binds the hearers to believe. So God, through Moses, confronted Pharaoh with various signs ([[Exodus 7 >> Bible:Exodus 7]]-[[Exodus 10 >> Bible:Exodus 10]]); through Jeremiah he foreshadowed his people's coming ruin by a girdle ([[Jeremiah 13 >> Bible:Jeremiah 13]]). Such is the barber's razor ([[Ezekiel 5:1 >> Bible:Ezekiel 5:1]]); such the marriage with a harlot ([[Hosea 1:2 >> Bible:Hosea 1:2]]).
source_text:
XXI. Occulta est, qua Deus per legatos suos aliquid ut divinum aliis ita significat, ut signa quaedam adhibeat, quorum efficacia illos ad annunciandum impellat, hos vero ad credendum obstringat.
Sic Deus per Mosen Pharaoni variis signis, Exod. 7. 8. 9. 10. capp. per Jeremiam populo suo eventuram illi perditionem cingulo praefigurat Jer. 13. Talis est novacula tonsoria, Ezech. 5. 1. Tale matrimonium cum scorto Hosee 1. 2.
